o1.biggest_strength: The trigger logic is the tightest: each habit email fires on the step before it, has a day-based fallback and a skip rule, and a no-same-day rule prevents collisions.
o1.biggest_mistake: Email 5 keeps a softened team-invite email for every user, even though shared projects retain only 34% and the tool cannot tell who has already shared.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Replace the day-10 sharing email with one that reinforces the habits or gates Pro, and drop the stray '(test: ...)' alternates in the subject lines so the copy is paste-ready.

o2.biggest_strength: It builds the whole series around the two habits and drops the team invite entirely; the Pro email goes only to users who formed a habit, and the drop list ties projects and labels to the 'perfect on Sunday, gone by Wednesday' trap.
o2.biggest_mistake: There is no fallback for users who never add a first task, so they skip the recurring-task email. The fixed day-3 device email can also land on the same day as the 3-day-inactive email, with no rule to space them.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Add a day-2 fallback for email 2 and a rule against two emails on one day, and confirm that 'reminders' is really a Pro-only feature before claiming it.

reason: Both are strong and the numbers check out. I'd take Output 2 because it fully drops the team invite and gates Pro behind the habits, though Output 1's trigger and fallback design is tighter.
